references.text: The Philistines gathered to offer sacrifices to Dagon, their god, and this verse continues the theme of praising one's god for victory over the enemy.
Samson killed a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone, which explains why the Philistines say he had 'multiplied their slain'.
Moses and Israel praised God after defeating the Egyptians, just as the Philistines here praise their god Dagon for victory over Samson.
The Philistines took the ark of the covenant to the temple of Dagon, but Dagon fell before the Lord's ark—a contrast to this situation where they believe Dagon has triumphed.
The Lord says He will not give His glory to other gods, which stands in contrast to the Philistines' praise of Dagon.
Nebuchadnezzar acknowledges that no one can stop God's hand, unlike the Philistines' mistaken belief that Dagon had overcome Israel's God.
